It is a disputed shrine (ronsha) of Aikamu-yama Shrine, a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} of Taki District in {{ill|Ise Province|Q864166|qid=Q864166}}. Its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== History ===
During the formative period of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yamato court}}, Takehiwake-no-Mikoto, who served as a kuni-no-miyatsuko (provincial chieftain) of the Ise and Kumano regions, governed the area around Tochihara. Together with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Mikoto}}, he came to be enshrined as the local tutelary deity sometime before the Edo period, and the shrine became known as “Takehiwake Shrine,” which is considered its founding origin. In the 40th year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} (1907), seven village shrines, four unranked shrines, and 59 subordinate shrines within the precincts of {{ill|Kawazoe|ja|川添村 (三重県)|ko|가와조에촌 (미에현)|qid=Q17176088|lt=Kawazoe Village}} were merged and the shrine was renamed “Kawazoe Shrine.”<ref name="県神社庁">{{Cite web|title=Prefectural Shrine Association – Kawazoe Shrine|url=https://jinja-net.jp/jinja-all/jsearch3all.php?jinjya=2885|access-date=December 18, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Prefectural Shrine Association – Kawazoe Shrine|url=https://jinja-net.jp/jinja-all/jsearch3all.php?jinjya=2885|access-date=December 30, 2025}}</ref>

Takehiwake-no-Mikoto · {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Mikoto}} · {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qid=Q455602}} · {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Oshihomimi-no-Mikoto}} · {{ill|Ame no Hohi|qid=Q10940685|lt=Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto}} · {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsuhikone-no-Mikoto}} · {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ikatsuhikone-no-Mikoto}} · and others, totaling thirty deities<ref name="県神社庁"/>

=== Rituals ===
* Annual festival: April 3
* Vernal Equinox Festival: Vernal Equinox Day
* Autumnal Equinox & Memorial Festival: Autumnal Equinox Day
* New Harvest Thanksgiving Festival: November 23
* Yakuyoke (misfortune prevention) & Celebration Report Festival: February 11
* Goshinkake Festival: The Sunday closest to February 19 (listed in “Special Shinto Rituals in Mie Prefecture”)
